segments.title: Chương 111: 0111【Số người dùng Xiaonei.com vượt 8000】
segments.content:
Chapter 114: CampusNet Users Surpass Eight Thousand

Waking up bright and early, Chen Guiliang went to the company.

Tailor shops could also make silk banners, but he didn't know where to find one.

An ordinary silk banner cost twenty to thirty yuan. Chen Guiliang needed to pick it up the same day, so he had to pay an extra rush fee, which brought the price up to 120 yuan per banner.

The company told him to come back in six hours.

At noon, Chen Guiliang treated Bian Guanyue's roommates to a meal. He also invited Senior He Qinqin, whom he had met on registration day.

"Our great talent, you've become quite famous at our school," He Qinqin joked as soon as she arrived.

Chen Guiliang asked, "Did someone post on CUEB's BBS?"

He Qinqin lamented, "Our school doesn't have a BBS, only an intranet forum and Baidu Tieba."

"Did anyone say anything bad about Chen Guiliang?" Bian Guanyue quickly asked.

He Qinqin said, "Yes. But most of them are mocking Peng Haoran. That guy used to be too high-profile and chased girls everywhere, only to dump them later. A lot of people have disliked him for a while now, so they're taking this opportunity to dig up dirt on him."

Bian Guanyue smiled, "That's good, then."

"You've become famous too," He Qinqin said. "Someone posted your photo on the CUEB Tieba, calling you our school's campus belle. They even said something about a femme fatale, causing a Peking University student and our school's big shot to fight over you."

"Those people are so boring," Bian Guanyue commented.

As they were talking, the five roommates arrived.

Chen Guiliang reminded the waiter to bring the food.

The person Bian Guanyue was closest to was her lower-bunk sister, named Fu Qiaoying.

Next was the dorm leader, Yu Wei.

"Thank you all for taking care of Guanyue. I'd like to toast all you older sisters." Chen Guiliang raised his drink.

They were all girls, so there was no alcohol today.

The lighting had been dim last night. Now, in the clearer light, the roommates were re-examining Chen Guiliang.

Mm, he really was quite handsome.

There was another girl named Liu Yu who chattered on about *Mengya* magazine and the New Concept Writing Competition, saying she had been very fond of literature in high school.

Halfway through the meal, Chen Guiliang began handing out business cards.

This was his third batch of business cards; the first two were almost all gone. The new cards didn't have his mobile number, only the company's landline.

He would continue to hand out cards with his mobile number in the future, but he would be more selective about who he gave them to.

Otherwise, his phone would be blowing up!

"You've opened two companies?" Lin Ruonan was even more excited.

Chen Guiliang briefly explained CampusNet, saying, "The internal testing will enter its second phase ahead of schedule at 12 PM tomorrow, opening up the friend invitation feature for users. For every friend successfully invited to register, you will receive corresponding 'Campus Coins'."

"Campus Coins" were part of the site's internal payment system, which was still far from perfect. You couldn't even top it up with money yet; you could only acquire coins through daily logins, inviting friends, and time spent online.

He Qinqin asked, "Is this like QQ's Q Coins?"

Chen Guiliang said, "Yes. You can't use them yet, but in the future, we'll introduce more homepage backgrounds, journal stationery, and background music. Some will be free, while others will require Campus Coins to purchase."

"CampusNet is still in its testing phase, so you must register with an invitation code. You can leave me your QQ number or email, and I'll send you an invitation code. When you invite your friends, you can also generate invitation codes to send them. A user can only generate 6 invitation codes."

Lin Ruonan said, "I'll give you my mobile number. Just send the website URL and invitation code to my phone."

"Alright."

Chen Guiliang took out his phone and noted down Lin Ruonan's number, but he didn't call on the spot. Instead, he sent a text message to the company.

A few minutes later, Lin Ruonan received a text message. It was from Guo Feng, with the URL and invitation code...

Lin Ruonan couldn't help but roll her eyes.

He Qinqin also got an invitation code. She found the website quite interesting. If it could become successful, she knew the founder, and maybe she could go work for Chen Guiliang in the future.

In the mid-afternoon, Chen Guiliang went to pick up the silk banners and delivered them to the Student Affairs Office and the dorm auntie.

When presenting the banners, he specifically had Bian Guanyue take a few photos.

The dorm auntie was very amusing; she even asked Chen Guiliang to have the photos developed and give her a copy.

Bian Guanyue was reluctant to see him go and walked Chen Guiliang to the bus station.

She had already learned how to knit and was working on a scarf, which would definitely be finished before Christmas.

The next day, at twelve noon, CampusNet launched its friend invitation feature.

But there was a limit on the number of invitations. One reason was to observe the rate of viral growth, and the other was to control the number of users to test stability.

Chen Guiliang stayed in the office for an hour and asked, "How many registered users are there now?"

Guo Feng stared at the backend data and said, "Total users are 1,137, with 328 currently online. It's the weekend, so the online rate is a bit high. Of those, 271 users registered in the last hour, and 104 of them went offline after registering."

"There will definitely be more people tonight," Chen Guiliang said.

Guo Feng smiled, "It's better if problems crop up now so we can fix the bugs early."

Dong Qianqiu said, "Are we just going to slowly work on the payment systems for CampusNet and Legends of the Three Kingdoms ourselves? Shouldn't we hire two more programmers?"

"It's still too early for charging," Chen Guiliang said. "Let's increase the user base first, then I'll go apply for a loan. With both projects combined, I can get a loan of up to 1 million yuan. Then we can hire more people."

In China's early internet market, payment processing was always a major issue.

Startups didn't have the capacity to build their own sales channels and had to rely on larger companies as agents. The agency fee was about one-third; if a user paid 100 yuan, the agent would take 33 yuan right off the top.

If the partnership went smoothly, that was acceptable.

But agents always liked to delay payments, dragging it out until you were at your wits' end.

Thanks to the trailblazer Shanda, the environment was much better now than it was three years ago, giving rise to many professional regional point-card agents. Even leasing servers for online games was pioneered by Shanda; before that, you had to buy your own servers.

Chen Guiliang planned to approach those regional point-card agents one by one to discuss cooperation after Legends of the Three Kingdoms and CampusNet had gained some popularity.

He also needed to talk to UnionPay and local banks about online banking payments.

Oh, and he had to work with mobile carriers like China Mobile and China Unicom to allow users to pay via SMS deductions. Those guys were the most predatory, taking a cut as high as 50-70%. The game company wouldn't take the loss, so the extra cost was passed on to the users. Anyone who topped up via SMS was a total sucker!

After sitting in the office for a while, Senior Sister Ao returned and slapped a pile of quotes on the table.

"Look at them yourself. I need a break," Ao Yanchen said, dead tired.

Chen Guiliang felt a little bad. The boss was out having fun with his girlfriend while the chief steward was working like a dog.

These were the quotes for the new office's renovation design, materials, and office supplies. Chen Guiliang scanned them carefully, felt there were no major issues, and picked up a pen to sign his approval.

Ao Yanchen said, "I asked around at the science park. The final inspection will be approved in a few days. We can already apply to start renovations on the office."

"The new home for our entire company will depend on you, Senior Sister Ao. Without you running around all day, we'd still be stuck in this old, shabby little place. You're our company's greatest contributor!" Chen Guiliang lavished her with emotional support.

Ao Yanchen wasn't buying it. "Salary!"

"Haven't we talked about salary yet?"

Chen Guiliang thought for a moment and, without trying to hide it from the other employees, said, "How about 5,000?"

"Deal." Ao Yanchen agreed instantly, very satisfied.

In 2004, the average salary for a new bachelor's degree graduate in China was only about 2,000 yuan.

For Peking University graduates, programmers and management trainees at foreign companies, as well as those in investment banking, had the highest salaries, ranging from 5,000 to 12,000 yuan.

However, only a few professions could earn that much at foreign companies.

Those who joined state-owned enterprises only made three to five thousand. Civil servants earned even less, just two to three thousand.

Peking University graduates who didn't do so well and joined small private companies earned about the same as civil servants.

Chen Guiliang's offer of a 5,000 yuan monthly salary for Ao Yanchen was equivalent to what she would earn starting at a large domestic company. It was even a bit high, considering she wasn't a technical talent and would have had to work her way up in an administrative role at a major domestic company.

If Ao Yanchen wanted stock options, she would have to further prove her value!

Chen Guiliang returned to his dorm to write, focusing on *Those Things in the Ming Dynasty*. If the loans for his incubated projects weren't enough, he would have to rely on royalties to hold out until venture capital came in.

At ten in the evening, Chen Guiliang called Guo Feng.

It was the weekend, so the student online rate was higher.

Guo Feng said, "The user growth at Peking University, Tsinghua University, and Renmin University has been particularly fast. It's already reached 2,132 people, and the current online rate is close to 40%. It seems... we don't need to do any on-the-ground promotion."

"How many from CUEB?" Chen Guiliang asked. "I only gave out 7 invitation codes to CUEB; the rest of the users came from their natural viral spread. And four of them don't even have computers."

Guo Feng said, "There are 39 registered users from CUEB. 32 of them were generated through natural viral spread in the last 10 hours."
